title: Restaurants & Ordering
description: Ordering, allergies and dietary restrictions. The allergy phrases are the ones worth being able to say without hesitating.

phrases.registerNotes: Said before every meal, alone or in company. Not saying it is the noticeable thing, not saying it.
phrases.animeNote: Anime gets this one right — it's used exactly as often in real life.

phrases.japanese: メニューをお願いします
phrases.registerNotes: 英語のメニューはありますか asks for an English one.
phrases.audioHint: メニューをおねがいします

phrases.japanese: アレルギーがあります

furigana.b: アレルギーがあります

phrases.registerNotes: Lead with this, then name the item. Worth having written on your phone in Japanese as well as spoken.
phrases.audioHint: アレルギーがあります

phrases.registerNotes: 〜が食べられません is the pattern — swap the food. Stronger and clearer than saying you don't like it.
phrases.audioHint: たまごがたべられません

phrases.registerNotes: The bookend to いただきます. Say it to staff on the way out and it lands as a genuine thank-you.
Reliably gets you the good thing, and reads as interest rather than helplessness.
phrases.audioHint: おすすめはなんですか

phrases.registerNotes: Water and tea are free and automatic at most restaurants — this is for a refill.

phrases.japanese: 豚肉は食べられません
phrases.registerNotes: Useful vocabulary to pair with it: 牛肉 (beef), 鶏肉 (chicken), 魚 (fish), 乳製品 (dairy), 小麦 (wheat), 落花生 (peanuts).
phrases.audioHint: ぶたにくはたべられません

phrases.japanese: これは何が入っていますか
phrases.romaji: kore wa nani ga haitte imasu ka
phrases.registerNotes: The follow-up to an allergy declaration. Dashi (fish stock) hides in a lot of apparently vegetarian food.
phrases.audioHint: これはなにがはいっていますか

phrases.japanese: お会計をお願いします
phrases.registerNotes: In many places you take the slip to the till rather than paying at the table.
phrases.audioHint: おかいけいをおねがいします
